about: Vectors of sealed conversations, docs/sealed.md (version 1). Generated by services/onboarding/tools/sealed_vectors.py; do not edit by hand. Every key here is a test key made from its name. Compare ids and keys as lower-case hex; compare 'devices' in the order of the head roster's device tags. An opened rumor is compared on pubkey, created_at, kind, tags, content and the id the opener computes. Signatures were made with fixed auxiliary randomness and only need to verify.

history_packing.name: 300 short rumors and one that cannot be shared
history_packing.note: Bob shares 301 rumors with Alice, oldest first: rumor i (0 to 299) is kind 14, created_at T0+i, from alice when i is odd and bob when even, one p tag (the other of the two), content 'Message <i>: "quoted" \ and é' (a double quote, one backslash and a non-ASCII letter: each counts as it is escaped). After rumor 149 comes one more from bob with 39 700 'x' as content: it fits a sealed rumor of its own but no kind 8564, whose JSON would pass the ceiling with it alone, so it is left out. Each 8564 is kind 8564, pubkey bob, created_at T0+800, tags [['p', alice]], content {"v":1,"rumors":[…]} in compact JSON with each rumor's keys in the order pubkey, created_at, kind, tags, content, id; the 8564's own keys in the order kind, pubkey, created_at, tags, content, id. 200 rumors are never reached here: with two 64-character fields each, 200 rumors are already more than 40 000 bytes.

ceiling.note: The bytes are those of the exact JSON string that is encrypted in the seal, as UTF-8. Here: compact JSON (no spaces), UTF-8 not escaped, the keys in the order pubkey, created_at, kind, tags, content, id. The content is described (a string repeated), not written out. For a rumor that fits, seal and wrap were made with the keys alice_phone → bob_lb1 and the fixed values of the case (see 'fixed'), so wrap_id can be reproduced; the lengths are those of the two NIP-44 payloads (base64 characters).

link.name: a request with the link's proof
link.note: link = hex HMAC-SHA256(key: the 32 bytes of the link secret, message: the 32 bytes of the device's public key).

link.name: a proof made with another secret
link.note: The request's link tag does not match the code this device showed.

link.name: a proof made for another device
link.note: The tag was copied from the tablet's request into the laptop's.

history.note: Bob shares his conversation with Alice to her new letterbox.

history.name: a rumor of a conversation the sharer is not in
history.note: The third rumor is between Mallory and Alice: Bob is neither its author nor in its p tags. It is dropped; the two others are added.

ready.note: sessions = GET /api/me/sessions (only the fields that matter are shown). Counted = chat true and last_activity within the last 30 days. The roster may carry ready when every counted session's client_pubkey is one of its devices.

cases.name: every chat session is a device
cases.note: Two chat sessions, both in the roster.

cases.name: a chat session that is not a device
cases.note: The tablet signed in two days ago and is not in the roster yet.

cases.name: another app's session never counts
cases.note: A session with chat false is not a device and does not hold ready back.

cases.name: a chat session idle for more than 30 days does not count
cases.note: The laptop was last active 31 days ago.

cases.name: a chat session active 29 days ago counts
a chat session with no client key counts and is no device
cases.note: client_pubkey is null (a session not bound to a key yet), active yesterday.

cases.name: a chat session that was never active does not count
cases.note: last_activity is null: not 'within the last 30 days'. (The most literal reading of §6; flagged to the contract's author.)
